name: item_acen_primary_of_three
description: Frozen reference behaviour: with three items selected, the shared action centre follows the DISTINGUISHED (primary) item — not the first one selected, not the mean of the set, not the set's bounding-box centre, and not the extreme along any axis. The rig places the distinguished item BETWEEN the other two on X so that 'primary' is separable from 'last in scene order' and from 'the extreme one', which an earlier rig could not do.
source: Frozen reference capture (headless, scripted). Rig rebuilt so the five candidate laws predict five distinct points.

provenance.harness: private headless capture harness (scripts + per-case result JSON live in the private tree)
provenance.notes: Seven consecutive evaluated frames, all identical, under two different transform configurations. Selection order is load-bearing: set on the first item, then ADD the second, then ADD the third, so the distinguished item is the LAST one added while sitting geometrically in the middle.

rig.comment: Three items, each carrying a unit cube so that every rejected candidate is genuinely computable from real geometry rather than degenerating to the origin.

why_this_matters: The primary sits at X=2, between 0 and 6. 'Midpoint of the set' would ALSO be a plausible reading of a centre that lands between the extremes — it is not, it is 3. Recording the four rejected numbers here is what stops a future reader re-deriving 'midpoint' from the single value 2.

classification.detail: vibe3d's item-mode action centre reads the primary layer's world pivot and produces (2,0,0) on this rig — identical to the reference, and different from all four rejected candidates. This fixture is a LIVE test that must pass.
